references.text: The next verse reminds us that it is the Lord who gives the power to gain wealth, as a direct correction to the pride expressed in verse 17.
Moses warns again against thinking in one's heart that one's own righteousness has brought success, the same theme of self-righteous pride.
The king of Assyria boasts that his own hand and wisdom have accomplished great things, an example of the pride Deuteronomy warns against.
The prince of Tyre says that his wisdom and understanding have brought him wealth, parallel to pride in one's own strength.
Habakkuk describes how the enemy attributes their strength to themselves and their own god, parallel to self-reliance without God.
Paul asks what you have that you did not receive, a correction to the idea that you achieved something by your own power.
James warns against boasting about future plans and merit without acknowledging God's will, the same theme of human pride.
